Byomkesh.description: A renowned Bengali detective known as a 'truth-seeker' or 'satyanweshi', who investigates mysteries with keen observation and logic.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler who narrates their adventures, assists in investigations, and is married to Satyaboti.

Satyaboti.description: Ajit's wife, mentioned as being away in Darjeeling.

Sukumar.description: Satyaboti’s brother, who takes her and her child to Darjeeling.

Nishanath Sen.description: The owner of Golap Colony and a former sessions judge from Bombay who runs a flower and dairy farm near Calcutta.

Damayanti.description: Nishanath Sen's wife, a graceful and efficient woman with a mysterious background and complex past.

Bijoy.description: Nishanathbabu's nephew and ward, in charge of the flower stall, emotionally involved with Bonolokhhi and previously with Mukul.

Panugopal.description: A young, hearing-impaired and speech-impaired man who manages the dairy at Golap Colony.

Bhujangadhar Das.description: A former doctor specializing in plastic surgery, debarred for a felony, now the farm's doctor and a key figure in the mystery.

Mushkil Mian.description: The farm's coachman, formerly a motor car driver, known for his catchphrase 'the problem is...'.

Rashiklal De.description: Manager of the vegetable stall at Hogg Market, a discontented man with a physical disability.

Sunayana.description: A mysterious ex-film actress also known as Netyakali, who is central to the investigation and acted in 'The Golden Maid'.

Indu Roy.description: A scriptwriter and Ajit's friend in the film world.

Ramen Mullick.description: A film enthusiast and 'encyclopedia' of the film world, who provides information about Sunayana.

Gourharibabu.description: Owner of Gourango Studios, who gave Sunayana her first film role.

Murari Dutta.description: A wealthy jeweller from the Dutta and Das family, murdered in mysterious circumstances involving Sunayana.

Tarok Ganguly.description: Director of 'The Golden Maid', the second film in which Sunayana acted.

Nazarbibi.description: Mushkil Mian’s second wife, originally from western India, in charge of the farm’s poultry.

Professor Nepal Gupta.description: A former chemistry professor with a scandalous past now conducting experiments at Golap Colony; he is the father of Mukul.

Mukul.description: Nepal Gupta's daughter, a hardworking young woman who manages the kitchen, with a past connection to the film world.

Brojodas.description: A former clerk turned Vaishnav devotee, who manages the cattle and dairy after a stint in prison.

Bonolokhhi.description: A young woman with a troubled past, skilled in tailoring, who becomes central to the mystery.

Putiram.description: Ajit and Byomkesh's domestic help, mentioned in connection with preparing food.

Dr Nagendra Pal.description: A local doctor called to examine Nishanathbabu after his death.

Pramod Barat.description: Inspector of the local police station who assists Byomkesh in the investigation alongside his subordinate Bikash.

Bikash.description: A police officer under Inspector Barat, who helps investigate No. 19 Mirza Lane.

Gaffoor Sheikh.description: Kanpur's shoe store owner in Calcutta, related to Mushkil Mian's second wife.

Calcutta.description: The capital city of West Bengal, India, where Byomkesh and Ajit reside.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, known for its tea gardens and cool climate.

Harrison Road.description: A prominent street in Calcutta, where Byomkesh and Ajit live.

Golap Colony.description: The name of Nishanath Sen’s farm, meaning 'Rose Colony', located near Mohanpur.

Mohanpur.description: A village near Calcutta, where Golap Colony is situated.

24 Paraganas.description: A district in West Bengal, referenced as the location of Golap Colony.

Sealdah.description: A major railway station in Calcutta, used for travel to Mohanpur.

Bombay.description: Now Mumbai, a major city in India, where Nishanathbabu served as a judge.

Bagbazaar.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta, location of the Dutta and Das jewelry store.

Dutta and Das.description: A famous jewellers' company in Calcutta, associated with Murari Dutta.

Gourango Studios.description: A film studio in Calcutta where Sunayana began her acting career.

The Poison Tree.description: A famous novel by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, adapted into a film starring Sunayana.

Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.description: A renowned Bengali novelist, author of 'The Poison Tree'.

The Golden Maid.description: A film directed by Tarok Ganguly, featuring Sunayana.

Hogg Market.description: A well-known market in Calcutta, where Golap Colony has a vegetable stall.

China town.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta known for its Chinese community, where Bhujangadhar once had a dispensary.

St Martha’s Girls’ School.description: An English-medium girls’ school in Calcutta attended by Damayanti Devi.

Nabadwip.description: A town in West Bengal, famous as a center of Vaishnavism, where Brojodas is found.

Mirza Lane.description: A street in Calcutta where Bhujangadhar and Bonolokhhi have a secret hideout.

Cafe Shahjahan.description: A restaurant in Calcutta where Byomkesh eats.

Anandabazaar.description: A leading Bengali newspaper, read by Ramenbabu.

Mohamudgar.description: A Sanskrit poem by Adi Shankaracharya, recited by Bhujangadhar.

Adi Shankaracharya.description: A revered Indian philosopher and theologian, author of 'Mohamudgar'.

Malkauns.description: A raga in Indian classical music, played by Bhujangadhar.

Gaur Sarang.description: Another raga in Indian classical music, played by Bhujangadhar.

Animal Farm.description: A reference to George Orwell’s novel, used humorously by Byomkesh for a cattle farm.

Sajjandas Mirzapuri.description: A fictitious criminal name used by Byomkesh as a ruse.

Banga Bilash Hotel.description: A hotel near Sealdah station where Rashik De is arrested.

Kanpur.description: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, referenced as the origin of Mushkil Mian’s wife's family.

babu.description: A respectful suffix used for men in Bengal, akin to 'Mr.'

kurta.description: A traditional loose-fitting shirt worn in India.

muslin.description: A fine, lightweight cotton fabric, often used for stoles or garments.

charpoy.description: A traditional Indian woven bed or cot.

rook.description: A chess piece, also called a castle.

rasgulla.description: A popular Bengali sweet made of cheese balls soaked in syrup.

beedi.description: A thin, hand-rolled Indian cigarette made of tobacco wrapped in a tendu leaf.

pyjamas.description: Loose-fitting trousers, traditional Indian attire, also used for sleepwear.

dhoti.description: A traditional men's garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

lungi.description: A casual lower garment worn around the waist, common in South Asia.

sherbet.description: A sweet, chilled drink, often fruit-flavored, popular in India.

ashram.description: A spiritual hermitage or communal living place, often associated with simplicity.

tilak.description: A mark, often of sandalwood paste, worn on the forehead as a religious symbol.

Vaishnav.description: A devotee of the Hindu god Vishnu, often marked by specific symbols and practices.

raga.description: A melodic framework in Indian classical music.

alaap.description: An improvised, unmetered introduction to a raga in Indian classical music.

kheer.description: A traditional Indian rice pudding dessert.

barfi.description: A sweet confection made from condensed milk and sugar.

chutney.description: A condiment made from fruits or vegetables, often sweet and tangy.

talaq.description: The Islamic practice of divorce, pronounced by the husband.

purdah.description: The practice of female seclusion or veiling in some South Asian communities.

sindoor.description: A red powder applied in the hair parting by married Hindu women.

namaskar.description: A respectful greeting or farewell in India, similar to 'namaste'.

paan.description: A preparation of betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

almirah.description: A cupboard or wardrobe, often used for storing valuables or clothes.

cheroot.description: A type of cigar, often smoked in India and Burma.

moong dal.description: A type of lentil commonly used in Indian cooking.

ghee.description: Clarified butter used in Indian cuisine.

sitar.description: A plucked stringed instrument used in Indian classical music.

thumri.description: A genre of semi-classical Indian music, often romantic or devotional.

sloka.description: A verse, phrase, proverb, or hymn, especially in Sanskrit literature.

bangle.description: A rigid bracelet, usually made of glass, metal, or plastic, worn by women in South Asia.

lassi.description: A traditional Indian yogurt-based drink, often sweet or salted.

paan stall.description: A small shop or kiosk selling paan and related items.

Kakababu.description: A respectful term for an elder male, often used for an uncle.
